title: Roast carrots and chickpeas with kale, feta and orange

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every item is a plain whole food or a simple staple such as tinned chickpeas, feta, honey and pumpkin seeds, with nothing factory-built.

supermarket.reason: Carrots, chickpeas, kale, feta, an orange and pumpkin seeds are everyday items at any Tesco at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a grater and a small bowl, and the technique is simple roasting and whisking.

works.reason: 750g carrots, two tins of chickpeas, 150g kale and 200g feta make a sensible lunch for four, and 33 minutes at 200°C will cook chunky carrots and crisp the kale.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to peel and chunk the carrots, drain the chickpeas, tear the kale and make the dressing, and the 25 plus 8 roasting minutes match the 33 printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm roast traybake suits mid-December, and the carrots are the bulk and point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no fancy language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Roast vegetables, chickpeas, kale, seeds and feta make a filling, balanced meal a family would happily eat again.
